To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the hierarchical Extreme Learning Machine network with trans-layer representation learning is a simple yet powerful method for unsupervised learning of visual features from massive unlabeled image data.

ELM-AEs are able to learn the local receptive fields at the lower layers and transfer them to the higher layers, and the trans-layer representations are able to learn translation and rotational invariant features.
the proposed method can learn hierarchical representations with much less time and with comparable or even better performance compared to other state-of-the-art methods.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the following aspects: (1) The proposed hierarchical ELM-AE networks are much faster to train compared with deep learning methods with complex architectures.
the design of a novel deep learning model, the ELM-AE network, which can learn a more complete representation with much faster learning speed than traditional deep learning methods.
the design of a hierarchical Extreme Learning Machine architecture to achieve unsupervised feature learning from massive unlabeled image data.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the proposed method is a promising alternative to the deep learning models for unsupervised feature learning and high-level tasks.
the proposed method is very competitive to the state-of-the-art unsupervised learning algorithms and deep learning models.
the proposed trans-layer representations with ELM-AEs based learning are very promising and competitive for unsupervised learning and high-level recognition tasks.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the trans-layer representation method can be applied to a wide variety of tasks with a simple network architecture.
the proposed method can be used as a powerful tool for unsupervised feature learning and representation learning, and the learned representations can be used in many applications.

the proposed trans-layer method can be used to replace the last layer of a standard Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) to form a new network with much faster learning speed, which can achieve competitive performance to the original network.
The main takeaway from our work is that

ELM-AE can learn local receptive fields as filters, which are similar to those learned by deep learning methods, but the training time for ELM-AE is only about 1/100 of that for deep learning methods.
a simple but powerful ELM-AE can learn good local receptive filters and a trans-layer can learn a more complete representation from these filters, which is very effective for high-level tasks.
ELM-AEs can be used as the learning unit in deep architectures to learn local receptive filters at each layer.
